findings.summary: The store has no locking, so if the purge job runs on a separate thread from handlers, a concurrent revoke can pop a token mid-purge, causing a KeyError in purge and leaving _items inconsistent with _by_token.

list.remove and del by index are O(n), so purging k sessions is O(n·k) and revoke does a linear scan with dataclass equality checks, which may be slow if _items grows large; rebuilding the list with a filter is suggested.
